title: Four Knights Scotch | The Sensei Speedrun | GM Naro

moves.spoken: The knight to f3, and we continue developing as Black brings out the knight to c6.
We continue with the Four Knights, heading for the Scotch — it's performed very well for us so far.
d4 — the Scotch break. We still haven't faced the main line, which is the bishop to b4 or the bishop to c5.
Black takes and we recapture with the knight on d4. Most players below 1500 tend to grab the knight here.
Black takes the knight on d4 — but that's not a good move, as we've discussed several times.
We recapture with the queen, which enters the center. Now a lot of players reflexively want to play c5 to attack it, thinking they gain something.
Instead Black plays d6. Note the bishop to b5 with check would be an empty gesture, because c6 just kicks it and we've gained nothing.
So the bishop goes to c4, and Black develops the bishop to e7.
Black castles. Now the other bishop is a trickier question.
I don't like the bishop to d2 — it's passive and blocks the d-file, where we'll want a rook. So b3, planning to fianchetto.
